difficulty_reason: For a locally ringed space X and a short exact sequence E_1 -> E_0 -> F -> 0 with E_1 and E_0 locally free of ranks r_1 and r_0, the lemma asserts a canonical map wedge^{r_0-r_1}F -> wedge^{r_1}(E_1^vee) otimes wedge^{r_0}E_0 which is an isomorphism at a stalk x if and only if F is locally free of rank r_0 - r_1 in a neighbourhood of x (statement lines 7726-7771). The proof first disposes of r_1 > r_0, where the left side vanishes by convention and no isomorphism is possible, so r = r_0 - r_1 >= 0 (proof lines 7743-7746). The map is then defined by an explicit formula on wedges using a local basis t_1, ..., t_{r_1} of E_1, the dual basis and local lifts of the s_i, and the author states that the proof that this is well defined is omitted (proof lines 7748-7760). If F is locally free of rank r it is straightforward to verify that the map is an isomorphism; conversely, if the map is an isomorphism at the stalk x, then wedge^r F_x is invertible, which forces F_x to be generated by at most r elements and hence the map alpha to have maximal rank modulo m_x, which then holds in a neighbourhood, giving local freeness of F of rank r (proof lines 7762-7771). Turning the invertibility of a top exterior power into a rank condition on alpha and then spreading maximal rank to a neighbourhood is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2; the omitted well definedness verification is recorded verbatim in the notes.
